h1: The 5 Best Removable Monitor Privacy Screens of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Removable Privacy Screens: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five removable monitor privacy screens in 22, 24, 27 and 32 inch sizes, compared by mount style, pack size and aspect ratio.
summary: The Peslv 2-pack for 24 inch 16:9 monitors is the best removable privacy screen for dual desks, with tab clips and a pair of filters. SightPro offers a single 24 inch filter for less. The 27 inch pack, the Vxaop 16:10 filter for 22 inch panels and a 32 inch filter with anti-glare complete the list.
intro: The classic privacy filter mistake is the aspect ratio. Two monitors both sold as 24 inch can have different shapes, and a 16:9 filter on a 16:10 panel leaves a visible gap or will not fit at all. Get the shape right before you worry about anything else on the listing.

We reviewed five removable privacy filters and ranked them on size coverage, mount style and pack count. Our source facts do not state viewing angle or brightness effects, so those need checking on the live page. The ranking therefore rewards clear fit information and a mount you can take off.

products.name: Peslv [2-Pack] 24 Inch Privacy Screen for Computer Monitor, Removable Tab Mount
products.verdict: A 24 inch, 16:9 two-pack with a traditional removable tab mount.
products.description:
The Peslv is a two pack of 24 inch, 16:9 privacy filters that attach with removable tab clips, listed in the $50 to $100 bucket. Tab clips are the most familiar way to fit a filter that you can take off again when you need to show someone your screen.

It takes first place because a pair covers two monitors, which is how many desks are set up. The SightPro below shares the mount style and size but is a single unit at a lower price, so it is the better choice only for one screen. The 27 inch pack requires bigger monitors.

Buy it for a dual 24 inch desk. Confirm your panel is 16:9 first. The caveats are the higher price bucket and an unlisted viewing angle.

products.name: SightPro 24 Inch 16:9 Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Removable Tab Mount
products.verdict: One 24 inch filter for a single monitor, in a lower price bucket.
products.description:
SightPro sells one 24 inch filter, shaped 16:9, that attaches with removable tab clips, and it falls in the $25 to $50 bucket. It uses the same mounting approach as the Peslv.

It ranks second because it covers only one monitor, though it costs less. If you ever upgrade to a dual setup, you need to buy a second filter, and the total may exceed the Peslv pack price. For a single screen, that is no concern.

It suits single monitor owners at standard 24 inch size. Skip it if you have two screens, since the pair from Peslv is simpler. The caveat is that the listing provides no viewing angle figure, so check that on the product page before deciding that it offers enough privacy for your office.

products.name: [2 Pack] 27 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Removable Tab Mount
products.verdict: A 27 inch, 16:9 two-pack with removable tab clips.
products.description:
This 27 inch, 16:9 privacy filter pack contains two filters with removable tab clips, in the $50 to $100 bucket. It mirrors the Peslv on mount style and pack size, only for bigger monitors.

It ranks third because its audience is narrower: it only fits 27 inch 16:9 screens. If your monitors are that size, it is the right pack and beats buying two singles. If they are not, it is simply the wrong shape.

Buy it for a dual 27 inch setup. Measure your screen diagonal and check the aspect ratio before ordering, since 27 inch monitors come in more than one shape. The caveat is the higher price bucket, which is in line with the Peslv, and the unlisted viewing angle.

products.name: Vxaop [2-Pack] 22 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Removable, 16:10
products.verdict: The 16:10 option for 22 inch monitors, as a two-pack.
products.description:
The Vxaop is a two pack of 22 inch, 16:10 privacy filters with a removable mount, listed in the $25 to $50 bucket. Its 16:10 shape is the point, since a 16:9 filter does not fit these panels cleanly.

It ranks fourth because it addresses a niche. For 22 inch 16:10 monitors, though, it is the only matching pick on this list, and it comes as a pair for a lower price than the Peslv. The listing does not state the mount style as clearly as the tab clip models.

Buy it if your monitors are 22 inch and 16:10. Others should skip it. The caveats are the niche size and the unlisted mount detail, so confirm how it attaches and how easily it comes off before you order.

products.name: [2026 New] 32 Inch Computer Privacy Screen Filter, Removable Tab Mount
products.verdict: A 32 inch filter with anti-glare and blue-light filtering.
products.description:
This 32 inch, 16:9 privacy filter has a removable mount, plus anti-glare and blue-light filtering features, in the $25 to $50 bucket. It is the largest screen size in the ranking.

It lands last because it combines the largest size with fewer standard compatibility details, and the listing does not state the pack count. The bundled anti-glare and blue-light claims are a bonus, but they are listing features rather than things we confirmed.

Buy it if you have a 32 inch monitor that needs a removable filter. Skip it if you need a two pack. The caveat is that 32 inch screens come in several shapes, so check your own panel's aspect ratio before ordering, and treat the added coating claims as marketing until you read the page.

whatMatters.detail: Aspect ratio is the width to height shape of the screen, such as 16:9 or 16:10. It matters because a mismatch leaves gaps or will not fit at all. Check your monitor's ratio in its manual or settings, then compare it with the filter's title.

Screen size is the diagonal measurement of the panel, such as 24 or 27 inches. Filters are cut to these sizes, and an off size filter will not cover the glass. Look up your monitor's exact diagonal, and do not guess from the label on the box.

Mount style is how the filter attaches. Tab clips or hooks let you remove it, which matters if you want to share your screen with a colleague. Look for removable wording in the listing, as the Peslv and SightPro show, and avoid adhesive styles if you want to switch it back.

Pack size is the number of filters in the box. Some listings sell single units and others two packs. It matters for dual monitor desks, where a pair costs less than two singles. Match the count to your screens before ordering.

Viewing angle describes how narrow the cone of visibility is, and it decides how private the screen really is. It is not in our source facts, so check the listing for a stated angle and read how the filter affects brightness from straight on.

faq.q: Will the filter fit my monitor?
faq.a: Match the diagonal and the aspect ratio. A 24 inch 16:9 monitor suits the Peslv or SightPro, while a 16:10 screen needs a 16:10 filter such as the Vxaop.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Ignoring aspect ratio. Two 24 inch monitors can be different shapes, so check your panel's specs before choosing the Peslv, the 27 inch pack or the 32 inch filter.
Only for two monitors. For a single 24 inch screen, the SightPro costs less, and buying the Peslv pair means a spare filter you will not use.
Most use removable tab clips, according to the listings, including the Peslv, SightPro and 27 inch pack. Align the filter over the screen, then hook the tabs behind the bezel and check for gaps.
Use a soft cloth and follow the maker's care guidance. Avoid harsh chemicals on the anti-glare 32 inch filter, and take the filter off to clean it if the tabs allow it.
Our facts do not cover brightness, so check the listing. Privacy filters in general reduce brightness somewhat, which is how they narrow the viewing angle, so you may need to turn the screen up.

finalTake: Match diagonal and aspect ratio first, then pick the pack size. The Peslv suits a dual 24 inch desk, and the SightPro covers a single screen for less. Owners of 27 inch or 32 inch panels have their own options, and anyone with a 16:10 monitor should go straight to the Vxaop.
